title: Say what produced every number
statement: Label every number and claim with what produced it, its grader, version, attempts, sample, scope and evidence class, and word the claim no more strongly than that evidence covers.
example: One project held seven classes of evidence side by side, from schema-only runs to partial live re-scores, and mixing them caused false confidence.
detail: An action packet in the solver lab required every generation artifact and summary to record its endpoint, model route, deployment health, number of attempts, judge model, bank use, fallback mode, runtime assets, evaluator version, sample size and proof class. The reason given: the project held schema-only, spread-sample, targeted-repair, archived, self-evaluated, older-grader and partial live evidence side by side, and mixing those proof classes 'caused false confidence in earlier work'. Its pass gate was that a new summary can be read without context and say what exactly was measured, and the parallel lab's takeaway was that the best evidence always says which evaluator version, endpoint mode and fallback mode were active. The label names the grader and its version, the build and route, the number of attempts and what picked among them, any bank or fallback, the sample size, the scope and the evidence class.
against: For delivery, the serving side treats a cached fallback as the right path for item types that fail badly, a degraded mode that returns known-good items; that serves a student, but it is not a measure of new content. The audit itself found no drift yet.
